MOD belongs in the thermal-infrastructure lane; its Airedale cooling capacity agreement suggests data-center cooling can be a capacity-constrained second-order node.

MYRG should be retained for later layers as a direct underfollowed electrical-construction and substation/data-center C&I exposure with disclosed backlog.

POWL, MOD, NVT, IESC, and STRL appear relevant but may now sit above the preferred $300M-$10B discovery filter or have rising attention; evaluate them as context or large-cap pure-play exceptions in a separate pass.

Add POWL as a high-priority underfollowed-ish electrical-equipment candidate for data-center power delivery: direct official evidence includes a greater-than-$400M behind-the-meter data-center order after fiscal Q2 2026.

For AI data centers, the chokepoint is not only total electricity supply; it also includes behind-the-meter power architecture, medium-voltage switchgear, substations, electrical construction labor and raceway/cable-management components.

Need a later pass on transformer-specific public equities and non-U.S./OTC names, because the strongest transformer bottleneck may sit in foreign-listed suppliers or diversified industrials rather than clean U.S.-listed small/mid-caps.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands a focused public-company universe for the AI data-center power bottleneck. The two-lane list keeps Vertiv as the obvious reference anchor, then prioritizes more underfollowed direct/second-order names in medium-voltage switchgear, grid/data-center electrical construction, and rack-level power/connectivity/cooling infrastructure. This is a research universe only, not a trading recommendation. Layer 1B expansion for the AI data-center power/grid chokepoint found one emerging reference supplier and three underfollowed discovery names. The strongest direct equipment signal is Powell Industries in medium-voltage switchgear and power-control systems. The underfollowed lane is concentrated in construction/EPC and grid-connection execution: MYR Group for transmission/substation work tied to data-center clusters, Primoris for behind-the-meter gas/microgrid, power delivery and utility infrastructure, and Modine for thermal capacity reserved by hyperscale data-center customers. This is research universe expansion only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
